header.running_head: Statements of the Sahabah (RA) Concerning the Evil of Dissension

blocks.text: The Chapter Concerning the Importance that the Sahabah (RA) Attached to Unity

This chapter highlights how the Sahabah (RA) attached great importance to unity in word and in deed and how they abstained from dissension and dispute in matters that had ramifications on Da'wah to Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ and matters of Jihaad.
Statements of the Sahabah (RA) Concerning the Evil of Dissension
The Statement of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Concerning Dissension

Ibn Is'haaq reports the historic sermon that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) delivered in the orchard of the Banu Saa'idah. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "It is not permissible for the Muslim to have two leaders. As soon as this happens, dissension springs up in all their affairs and all the commands issued. Their unity is then fragmented and they start to fight amongst themselves. At this point, the Sunnah is forsaken, Bid'ah rears is ugly head and anarchy intensifies. No one can then set matters right." [^1]
The Statement of Hadhrat Umar (RA) Concerning Dissension

In the narration discussing the scenario before the pledge of allegiance was taken at the hand of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Saalim bin Ubayd states that someone from the Ansaar said, "(Who do we not appoint) A leader from amongst us (Ansaar) and another from amongst you (Muhaajireen)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) responded to this by saying, "Two swords in one sheath!? They will never fit." [^2]
